check.vm_folder_unset: not set yet (chosen in the first-run assistant)
check.not_writable: {path} is not writable by this user
check.nm_ok: {path} hides kvmnet*, ks-* and vnet* interfaces
check.nm_reinstall: reinstall the kvm-studio package to get {path}
check.nm_missing:
{path} is missing or outdated: {app} networks show up in the network applet.
       To fix it: {command}
cli.help_mode: interface mode (default: [interface] mode from the configuration)
cli.help_check: check the configuration and the host, then exit
cli.help_reload: web mode: restart on code changes (development)
cli.help_no_browser: web mode: do not open the browser
cli.no_pywebview: pywebview is not installed. Use --mode web instead.
cli.no_web_engine: No web engine found for the window. Install python3-pyqt6-webengine (or webkit2gtk4.1), or start with --mode web.
cli.share_unavailable: share_on_lan is not available yet (planned for V1). Set [web] share_on_lan = false in the configuration.
cli.web_link: Open this link (it contains the session token): {url}
cli.backend_failed: the {app} backend did not start; see the messages above
cli.port_in_use: {error}. Change the port in Preferences > Interface.
uninstall.title: Uninstall {app}
uninstall.vms: Virtual machines created by {app}, and the files that would be deleted:
uninstall.always_kept: Always kept: ISO images, files used by other VMs, files outside the library.
uninstall.ask_vms: Delete these virtual machines and files?
uninstall.ask_vms_again: This cannot be undone. Really delete them?
uninstall.ask_networks: Delete the networks no remaining VM uses?
uninstall.package_failed: The package could not be removed ({error}). Run: sudo dnf remove kvm-studio
uninstall.package_removing: Removing the package (follow it with: journalctl -u kvm-studio-removal).
uninstall.iso_rights: Access rights given to virtual machines on your ISO libraries:
uninstall.ask_iso_rights: Take back the rights the helper added (those set before stay)?
uninstall.iso_failed: The helper did not answer: the access rights on the ISO libraries were left as they are.
close.why: They keep running after {app} closes: libvirt and QEMU run them, not {app}. You find them again the next time it starts.
close.stuck: These virtual machines are still running ({count}):
close.power_off_warning: Powering off is like pulling the plug: unsaved work in the guest is lost.
check.kvm_no_cpu_support: the processor shows no hardware virtualization: enable Intel VT-x or AMD-V in the firmware (BIOS/UEFI)
check.kvm_reboot_needed: the KVM modules of the running kernel ({kernel}) are no longer installed, most likely after a kernel update: restart the computer
check.kvm_module_not_loaded: the KVM module is not loaded: sudo modprobe {module}
check.kvm_no_dev_kvm: /dev/kvm is missing although {module} is loaded: restart the computer, then check: dmesg | grep -i kvm
check.kvm_dev_kvm_denied: /dev/kvm is not accessible to this account: log out and back in, then check: ls -l /dev/kvm
check.nested_off: disabled ({module}); only needed for hypervisors inside VMs: echo 'options {module} nested=1' | sudo tee /etc/modprobe.d/kvm-nested.conf, then restart
